transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Kim (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (NovaHealth ML Eng), Sana Iqbal (NovaHealth Product), Raj Patel (NovaHealth Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focusing on SDK integration with NovaHealth app, function/tool calling behavior, and structured JSON output. SE to run benchmarks, security clarifications around KMS and data residency, and plan next schema review.

Topics:
- SDK integration gotchas (retries, timeouts, streaming vs non-streaming)
- Function/tool calling semantics and how Redwood SDK surfaces them
- Structured output + schema validation and guarded parsing to avoid hallucinations
- Perf numbers observed and tuning (batching, KV cache, token limits)
- Security (KMS, SOC2, SSO, audit logs)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda — integration updates from Daniel, perf notes from Marcus, security check from Raj, and then next steps.
[00:12] Daniel: cool, uh yeah we've been wiring the Redwood SDK into our pipeline. using the node client, we implemented function calls for the report generator and structured output for the downstream ingestion. running into some weirdness with the schema — sometimes the model returns extra fields or leaves arrays empty.
[00:28] Marcus: that sounds like a common structured-output drift. Are you using the SDK's schema enforcement option or just post-validate?
[00:35] Daniel: post-validate right now. we tried the "schema" config but the validator seemed to drop nested fields occasionally. might be our setup.
[00:45] Marcus: got it. two quick things — one, when you use the SDK's function-calling wrapper, ensure you set explicit required fields in the function contract. that reduces hallucination where the model invents fields. two, enable strict parse mode (we exposed as parse_mode: "strict") which will put any unexpected props into an _extras field rather than breaking. also watch streaming vs non-streaming; streaming sometimes interleaves tool calls if you don't buffer.
[01:12] Sana: oh that streaming interleave — can you explain? we actually need partial results asap for our UI.
[01:18] Marcus: yeah so with streaming, tokens come as they are generated. if you're simultaneously calling a tool based on an intermediate token sequence, there's a race where the SDK might trigger a function call before it finishes the intended output. we recommend using a short buffer window or explicit end-of-turn token to signal tool invocation.
[01:37] Daniel: we're currently using a 200ms buffer, but maybe we need a heuristic — or set the SDK to only do function calls at full completion.
[01:44] Alicia: tradeoff there is latency vs correctness. if you wait for completion, response latency goes up. NovaHealth's SLO for UI is 300ms p95 right?
[01:51] Sana: target is 250ms p95 for inline suggestions, but reports can be slower.
[01:57] Marcus: then for inline suggestions we'd use a smaller model, and for final reports use a batch non-streaming endpoint with structured output enforcement. Redwood can route by model to keep latency low (hosted small model for suggestions, Dedicated for heavy report generation).
[02:12] Raj: security question — when function calls include PHI, how is that payload stored? we need to know whether KV cache or logs persist any sensitive payloads.
[02:21] Marcus: good call. by default Redwood's hosted API does not persist request bodies beyond short-term operational logging. Dedicated or Private modes give you control: KV cache (we note it sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in earlier docs) is optional and can be disabled, and you can configure encryption-at-rest with your KMS. audit logs are available via Redwood Console and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[02:46] Raj: and key management — do you support customer-managed keys in Dedicated?
[02:50] Alicia: yes, CMKs via AWS KMS or GCP KMS for Dedicated and Private. we support HSM integrations for on-prem if needed. we'll share the security packet with the exact rotation policy.
[02:59] Raj: please add our rotation window constraints — we rotate every 30 days and need a 72-hour pre-rotation notification.
[03:06] Alicia: noted.
[03:09] Marcus: back to perf — Daniel, you mentioned token counts spiking. can you share sample logs?
[03:15] Daniel: i've pushed a sample to the shared drive (link: https://redwood.example.com/shared/nova/payload-samples.csv) — some requests go from 300 tokens prompt to 4k because the model starts enumerating extra context.
[03:27] Marcus: two levers: prompt engineering to truncate non-essential context, or apply the SDK-level max_output_tokens and stop sequences. also we have a batching suggestion — when you run many report generations, use Redwood's batch endpoints or the SDK's batch helper which aggregates requests into efficient micro-batches. that significantly lowers cost but watch tail latency.
[03:50] Daniel: we tried batching, saw cost improvements but had a tail p99 increase.
[03:55] Marcus: expected. if you need strict latency SLOs, pin to Dedicated nodes and configure autoscale with burst capacity so you don't get queued (we'll include pricing for burst).
[04:06] Sana: about structured output — can we see an example schema enforcement? samples would help our product folks.
[04:12] Marcus: yes; we'll send a sample schema and an example response in strict parse mode. note that the SDK will return a parse_error field if the model returns something invalid, and you can opt-in to a best-effort repair mode which attempts to map fields but may introduce hallucination.
[04:29] Daniel: that repair mode worries me — we prefer fail-fast with a retry to the model or fallback to a previous cached answer.
[04:36] Marcus: that's easily configured; we can set fallback policies in the SDK: retry with a different model variant (smaller/larger), or fallback to cache. Redwood Optimize also suggests quantization/profile that might help.
[04:50] Sana: on the subject of model variants — can we automatically route by cost vs latency? our finance team wants default cheaper model and upgrade only for failures.
[04:59] Alicia: yes, smart routing policies let you define a priority list: try hosted small model first, if the quality metric fails then try Dedicated, or escalate regionally. we can demo the routing policy DSL.
[05:11] Raj: one more on compliance — do audit logs include redacted things, or do they contain full payloads? we need to show auditors.
[05:18] Marcus: audit logs can be configured at multiple levels: metadata-only, redacted payloads, or full payloads — for full you'll need Dedicated/Private with customer KMS. logs are forwardable to your SIEM.
[05:29] Daniel: ok, next on bench: our initial bench shows p50=140ms p95=420ms for small inline model, but report generation p50=780ms p95=2.3s. we want to lower report p95.
[05:41] Marcus: for report p95, use KV caching for repeated prefixes, batch gen for throughput, and possibly quantized model variants on Dedicated. also check tokenization differences — sometimes token counts differ between tokenizers.
[05:54] Daniel: noted.
[05:56] Alicia: actionable recap: Marcus runs a 1k benchmark end-to-end; Alicia sends pricing + security packet; Daniel shares function payloads and schema; Raj confirms KMS details.
[06:08] Sana: timeline sounds good. also can we get a short doc on function-calling patterns to avoid partial calls?
[06:14] Marcus: yes i have a patterns doc — will share link (doc: https://redwood.example.com/patterns/function-calls.md). it has examples for buffer windows, parse strategies, and retry semantics.
[06:27] Daniel: small note, transcription earlier in our internal notes mis-typed KV cache as K-V cash which caused a bit of confusion in the security review.
[06:35] Alicia: haha noted, we'll correct docs.
[06:38] Raj: any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:41] Marcus: none; we might need more logs to tune the batch size threshold.
[06:46] Daniel: i'll attach logs (link: https://redwood.example.com/shared/nova/bench-logs.tar.gz).
[06:53] Alicia: perfect. last thing — do we want to set a check-in after Marcus shares the benchmark?
[06:58] Sana: yes let's do a follow-up on 2025-08-13 to review results and the schema fixes.
[07:05] Alicia: great, i'll send calendar invite. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
